 MANILA — Singer and television host Karylle Tatlonghari has pushed back against the notion that a woman’s worth should be measured by whether she becomes a mother, describing the criticism she receives about parenthood online. 
 Speaking at a Nov. 9 media conference in Taguig City for the reality series  Manila Matriarchs , Karylle addressed comments questioning her life choices.  “Am I sayang? I don’t think so,”  she said, using a Filipino word that, in this context, conveys the idea of wasted potential. 
 The remarks highlighted a recurring subject in interviews with the  It’s Showtime  host, who married Sponge Cola vocalist Yael Yuzon in March 2014. 
 In 2018, Karylle discussed how women face pressure to have children, particularly during family gatherings, and said that talking to other women with similar experiences could provide support. In 2019, she said there was no single timetable for balancing a career and family, and described enjoying time with her husband while pursuing her work. 
 Karylle also publicly rejected pregnancy speculation in February 2025. Her latest comments concerned expectations placed on women and did not amount to an announcement about her private family plans. 
 Manila Matriarchs , which began streaming Nov. 10 on iWant, follows Karylle and three other women working across entertainment, fashion, art and business: Joanna Preysler-Francisco, Myrza Sison and Trisha Bantigue-Tsao. 
 The eight-part unscripted series was filmed in Metro Manila and San Francisco. According to the producers, it follows the participants’ careers and relationships while examining the demands of family life and public visibility. 
 Filipino American producer Cece Asuncion created the series, which is produced by Girl Bye Productions Inc. and Lucca Creatives. The first episode is available free worldwide on iWant, and the platform has announced additional episodes beginning Nov. 24.
